evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the 10–15 minute call structure or waited for a yes before diving into scheduling logistics. Jumped straight into availability checking.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving day (Wednesday Sept 30), city-to-city (Austin to Austin), and size (950 sq ft apartment) were gathered; name confirmed as Marie; but the rep never explicitly asked 'What city are you moving to?' — it emerged through scheduling rather than being asked upfront.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as 'Besides pricing. Do you have any questions and concerns with kind of instead of by dates if we can get that sorted out?' — this came after several minutes of scheduling probing, not before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer mentioned past move pricing: 'the last time I've used them, it was about the same pricing and I'm kind of estimating just by what happened last time.' Rep acknowledged ('Okay, and I can actually look up that last move') but did not dig deeper with 'tell me more about that' or explore what the concern actually was. Customer also expressed anxiety about glass items: 'I'm so scared is gonna get broken.' Rep empathized and shared her own story but never asked 'What specifically worries you about how movers handle fragile items?' — rapport without real follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledged concerns piecemeal but never said 'So what I'm hearing is...' or confirmed what was actually being worried about.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details: Gathered: property type (apartment), floor (3rd), rooms (2 bed), walk distance (20 ft), special items (washer/dryer, glass table, glass calendar, queen mattress, loveseat, entertainment center, TV, trundle bed, twin mattress, dresser, dining table, 10 boxes). Missing: number of rooms fully unpacked; additional stops (destination address floor/stories/access confirmed verbally but not confirmed in the structured probing section); walk distance at destination never asked.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Not offered. Packing was never mentioned as a service option.
evidence_quotes.box_count: Asked: 'And to book a block count for move this size is about 25 to 35 boxes. Do you think you fall within that range?' Customer answered 10 and under; rep did not probe whether customer might have items that could push over typical.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full: '$208 for two movers and 126 foot box truck' and estimated '4 to 5 hour range' with math: '$832 and if we were to hit the five...1040.' Personalized to prep level: 'the most important one is how well prepared you are...if you consolidate things in the boxes and even have the ability to take some of the smaller things over yourself...that really keeps the time down.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Mentioned 'no deposit required' and 'no charges or fees to cancel or change the date.' Mentioned hourly rate. Did NOT explicitly call out trip fees, overnight fees, packing materials, 2.5-hour minimum, or 15-minute-increment commitment upfront.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_silence: Not asked. Rep moved directly into 'do you want to go ahead and have us help you on with that move' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' and holding silence.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Full: 'we can't make it in the time window that we arrange. We immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Terms clearly stated (immediate discounting if late).
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage: Partial. Mentioned: 'we do have our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate that provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Missing: explicit framing that it's 'no deductible / no fine print' and that it's built into the rate (implied but not explicitly restated as a non-add-on given the proactive context).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep did not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. The two promises were mentioned but not looped back to the earlier concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway: 'Alright. And then do you have any other questions or concerns for me while you have me on the, on the line?' — generic, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Not asked. Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out. Asked 'do you want to go ahead and have us help you on with that move on Wednesday September 30th or do you want to go ahead and see if you can get that day off' — the second clause ('or do you want to go ahead and see if you can get that day off') is a built-in out, softening the ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Mentioned: 'no deposit required again on our schedule and then no charges or fees to cancel or change the date'.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: origin address (7707 South I-35 frontage road, Apt 736, Austin, TX), destination (5916, 1500 sq ft home), date (Wednesday Sept 30), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM). Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size confirmation (mentioned '$208 for two movers' but never explicitly asked 'Is two movers okay?'), crew notes about fragile items (washer/dryer, glass) mentioned but not confirmed as left for crew.

top_strength: Excellent logistics detail gathering and natural rapport—the rep elicited a full inventory of furniture and special items through conversational follow-up, and her empathetic response to the customer's glass item anxiety built genuine trust.
coaching_note: Start every call with a clean quid pro quo framing and wait for a yes before jumping into logistics; this call skipped the frame entirely and lost the structure that sets expectation and buys permission to dig deeper on concerns.
